title: Laurent polynomial ring
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $K(T)$ the field of rational functions [def-weil-rational-function-field]. The *Laurent polynomial ring* $K[T,T^{-1}]$ is the subring of $K(T)$ generated by $K[T]$ and $T^{-1}$: its elements are the finite sums $\sum_{m\in\mathbf Z}c_mT^m$ with $c_m\in K$, all but finitely many zero, equivalently the fractions $P/T^{k}$ with $P\in K[T]$ and $k\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. The coefficients $c_m$ of an element are uniquely determined (a Laurent polynomial is $0$ if and only if all its coefficients vanish, since $T^kf\in K[T]$ for $k$ large), so $K[T]\subset K[T,T^{-1}]$ is the subring of the elements with $c_m=0$ for $m<0$. For $f\in K[T,T^{-1}]$ and $c\in K^\times$, the substitution $f(cT^{-1})$ of [def-weil-rational-function-field] sends $\sum_mc_mT^m$ to $\sum_mc_mc^mT^{-m}$, hence maps $K[T,T^{-1}]$ into itself; in particular $P(cT^{-1})\in K[T,T^{-1}]$ for $P\in K[T]$. For a field extension $K\subset L$, the coefficientwise map $K[T,T^{-1}]\to L[T,T^{-1}]$ is an injective ring homomorphism which commutes with the substitutions $f\mapsto f(cT^{-1})$, $c\in K^\times$, and it is the restriction of the inclusion $K(T)\subset L(T)$. For $R\subset K$ a subring (such as $\mathbf Z\subset\mathbf Q$), $R[T,T^{-1}]\subset K[T,T^{-1}]$ denotes the Laurent polynomials with coefficients in $R$.

source.place: statement: 'the integral factors satisfy the Laurent-polynomial identity $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)$ in $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$', and ## Proof, step 3, 'as an identity in $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$'; the ring is used there without definition. The same ring is used in sk-thm-fe/prop-functional-equation.md, step 2, and in sk-thm-weil5/thm-weil-final-functional-equation.md.
